channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: New section of road to Rakhman springs opens in East Kazakhstan region
item.description: A 13-kilometer section of the Uskemen-Altai-Ulken Naryn-Katonkaragay-Rakhman springs road has been opened in the East Kazakhstan region. The project, completed between 2025-2026, includes new asphalt, drainage systems, and safety infrastructure, improving access to Katonkaragay National Park and tourist sites.

item.title: Taliban Begin Paving Farah-Farah Rud Road Project Valued at 982 Million Afghanis
item.description: The Taliban have commenced paving the Farah-Farah Rud road in Farah Province, a project costing over 982 million Afghanis. The 61-kilometer road is expected to be completed in 16 months and is intended to facilitate international trade. However, past development projects initiated by the Taliban have reportedly failed to address fundamental issues.

item.title: Flydubai Pilot Planned to Crash Plane into Ben Gurion Airport Terminal
item.description: An Omani pilot for flydubai allegedly planned to crash the aircraft into the Ben Gurion Airport terminal, according to Israeli Channel 12 journalist Amit Segal. The pilot reportedly attacked the captain over Jordan, intending to seize control. The plan was foiled when the injured captain opened the cockpit door.

item.title: Two Arrested in Fergana for Attempting to Sell 1kg of Narcotics for $20,000
item.description: Two individuals were apprehended in Fergana for attempting to sell one kilogram of narcotics for $20,000. A criminal case has been initiated against the two suspects, and investigative actions are currently underway.

item.title: Kazakh Judoka Sherzod Davlatov Wins Silver at World Championships in Baku
item.description: Kazakhstan's Sherzod Davlatov secured a silver medal at the senior World Judo Championships in Baku. He lost in the final of the under-60kg category to Azerbaijan's Ahmed Yusifov. Davlatov defeated notable opponents, including the world champion and Olympic bronze medalist Ryuju Nagayama of Japan, en route to the final.

item.title: Uzbekistan Customs Official: Situation in Afghanistan Worsens Drug Smuggling
item.description: An official from Uzbekistan's Customs Committee stated that the situation in Afghanistan has not improved, and large quantities of drugs continue to enter Uzbekistan. The official described the current drug situation as complex, with increased attempts to smuggle narcotics across the border. The source indicates ongoing challenges with drug trafficking from the neighboring country.

item.title: Kremlin Spokesperson Praises Kazakh President Tokayev's Political Strength
item.description: Dmitry Peskov, Russian presidential spokesperson, described Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev as a "politically very powerful man with enormous resources." Peskov stated that only leaders with strong political vision, firmness, and consistency can make such statements, referencing Tokayev's comments about Vladimir Putin.

item.title: Taliban and Pakistan to Join Moscow Format Talks on Afghanistan
item.description: Taliban and Pakistani officials will attend the eighth Moscow Format meeting on Afghanistan in Moscow. The talks will focus on political and economic ties, terrorism, and drug trafficking. Senior officials from regional countries, including China, India, Iran, and Central Asian nations, are expected to participate.

item.title: Search Continues for Missing South Korean Citizen in Almaty Mountains
item.description: Search operations are ongoing for a South Korean citizen who went missing in the Almaty mountains approximately one week ago. Rescuers are meticulously examining difficult terrain, steep slopes, and canyons. The Ministry of Emergency Situations reported that 88 personnel, 10 vehicles, three canine units, and seven drones are involved in the extensive search effort.

item.title: North Korea Conducts Successful Test of Hypersonic Missile Targeting 1,000 km Away
item.description: North Korea successfully test-fired a hypersonic missile that accurately hit a target 1,000 kilometers away, state media reported. Leader Kim Jong Un observed the launch, emphasizing the military's high skills and readiness for counterattacks. The test demonstrated the country's advanced missile capabilities.

item.title: Russia and US Discuss $20 Billion Deal for Lukoil Assets
item.description: Russia and the United States are reportedly discussing a $20 billion deal concerning Lukoil's foreign assets, including oil fields, refineries, and gas stations. American billionaire Todd Boehly is among the potential buyers. Boehly has reportedly donated $2 million to a political organization linked to Trump.

item.title: Taliban Foreign Minister Attends Eighth Moscow Format Meeting on Afghanistan
item.description: Amir Khan Muttaqi, the Taliban's Foreign Minister, traveled to Russia for the eighth "Moscow Format" meeting on Afghanistan. He is expected to discuss the current situation, regional cooperation, counterterrorism, and drug trafficking. Muttaqi will also hold a bilateral meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov.

item.title: Taliban Complete First Transit Road Linking Badakhshan and China
item.description: The Taliban announced the completion of the 121-kilometer Wakhan road in Badakhshan, connecting Afghanistan to China via the Wakhan Corridor. State media reported the road construction, costing 365 million Afghanis, was done in two phases. Taliban officials stated the route could boost trade, transit, and economic relations between Afghanistan, China, and regional countries.

item.title: Uzbekistan Energy Oversight Agency Reviews Nine-Month Performance
item.description: Uzbekistan's Inspectorate for the Use of Electric Energy, Oil Products, and Gas reviewed its January-September performance. The meeting, led by Inspectorate head Akhadkhon Isokzhonov, focused on improving control mechanisms, timely addressing identified shortcomings, and enhancing efficiency. Attention was given to regional outreach and handling entrepreneurs' appeals.

item.title: Public Transport System Modernized in Namangan with New Buses and Routes
item.description: Namangan region is enhancing its public transport system by importing 108 modern buses and implementing gross-contract routes. The fleet now totals 130 buses, with a growing share of eco-friendly vehicles. This initiative aims to improve service quality and create new jobs, as highlighted by regional officials.

item.title: Kazakh Defense Minister Inspects Military Unit in Akmola Garrison, Orders Improvements
item.description: Kazakhstan's Defense Minister, Major General Aidar Zhaxybayev, conducted a surprise inspection of a military unit in the Akmola garrison. He reviewed service organization and living conditions, specifically focusing on barracks and infrastructure. The minister issued directives to enhance the daily living conditions for servicemen.

item.title: OPEC+ Countries Maintain November Oil Production Levels
item.description: Seven OPEC+ countries have agreed to maintain their September oil production levels for November. The organization confirmed participants' commitment to full compliance with the cooperation declaration. The next meeting is scheduled for November 1, 2026. This decision impacts global energy markets and supply dynamics.

item.title: OPEC+ Countries to Maintain Current Oil Production Levels
item.description: OPEC+ countries will maintain their oil production levels from September and October into November. Seven member nations, including Kazakhstan, Russia, and Saudi Arabia, confirmed their commitment to voluntary production cuts through November 2026 during an online meeting. The group will continue monthly discussions on market conditions.

item.title: Poland and Romania Refuse to Aid Ukraine's Grain Exports
item.description: Poland and Romania have declined to assist Ukraine in exporting grain. Ukraine had sought help to transport more grain through Europe amid ongoing challenges with Black Sea exports. The decision was reported by Politico, citing the difficulties Ukraine faces in exporting its agricultural products.

item.title: Navoiy Mining and Metallurgy Combine reports $2.38 billion net profit from gold sales in six months
item.description: The Navoiy Mining and Metallurgy Combine announced a net profit of $2.38 billion from gold sales in the first half of the year. Despite a decrease in production volume, revenue increased by 57.2% due to rising gold prices, though production costs also rose sharply.

item.title: Ukraine, Russia, and US may hold new talks in late October, says Zelensky
item.description: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that the US has proposed a trilateral technical meeting with Ukraine and Russia in late October. Kyiv supports the initiative and awaits Moscow's response, with potential venues including the UAE or other US-suggested locations.

item.title: Regional alignment shifts: Pakistan-Taliban rift widens amid new alliances
item.description: A widening rift between Pakistan and the Taliban, coupled with intensified Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan threats, is reshaping Afghanistan's regional dynamics. New Delhi gains leverage as Pakistan's strategic depth calculation unravels. This occurs amidst evolving regional security landscapes, including the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey, and an upgraded India-Israel strategic partnership.

item.title: OPEC+ Countries Maintain Oil Production Levels for Second Consecutive Month
item.description: OPEC+ nations will keep oil production levels unchanged in October, matching September's output. Seven member countries, including Saudi Arabia and Russia, confirmed their commitment to the cooperation agreement during a virtual meeting. They will continue monthly analyses of the market situation, with the next meeting scheduled for November 1.

item.title: UN Reports Unexploded Ordnance Poses Serious Threat in Afghanistan's Kunduz Province
item.description: The UNDP is continuing efforts to clear explosive remnants and raise awareness about mines in Kunduz, Afghanistan. Unexploded ordnance remains a significant problem, requiring further action. The program aims to create safer environments in cooperation with international organizations and with support from the UN Special Trust Fund for Afghanistan.

item.title: Pakistani Representatives to Attend Moscow Format Meeting on Afghanistan
item.description: Representatives from Pakistan are scheduled to participate in the Moscow Format meeting concerning Afghanistan. This engagement highlights Pakistan's involvement in regional discussions aimed at addressing the situation in Afghanistan. Further details on the agenda and specific Pakistani representatives were not provided in the source.

item.title: Pakistan Airstrikes Prompt Residents of Helmand and Kandahar to Build Shelters
item.description: Following recent Pakistani airstrikes, residents in Afghanistan's Helmand and Kandahar provinces are building underground shelters and relocating due to fears of renewed attacks. Local sources report increased psychological pressure and concern among the population. Several families have reportedly left their homes, particularly those near military facilities, fearing they could be targeted.

item.title: OSCE Youth Media Camp Focuses on Countering Disinformation and Digital Security
item.description: A three-day youth media camp was held in Uzbekistan's Tashkent region, focusing on combating disinformation, media literacy, and digital security. Thirty university students participated in the event, organized by the OSCE Project Coordinator in Uzbekistan and the Journalists' Retraining Center.

item.title: Uzbekistan Exported $322.3 Million in Gas Over Eight Months, Imported $1.2 Billion
item.description: Uzbekistan exported $322.3 million worth of gas in the first eight months of the year while importing $1.2 billion. Despite a significant increase in imports, the government has not halted exports.

item.title: Taliban Foreign Minister Travels to Russia for Moscow Format Meeting
item.description: The Taliban's acting foreign minister has traveled to Russia to attend the Moscow Format meeting. The purpose of the meeting and the specific agenda were not detailed in the announcement. This engagement signifies a diplomatic outreach by the Taliban administration.

item.title: Kajaki Dam Electricity Cut Off in Kandahar and Helmand, Residents Face Shortages
item.description: Local sources report that electricity from the Kajaki Dam has been completely cut off in Kandahar and Helmand provinces. Residents now rely on expensive diesel and solar power, available only in limited amounts. Taliban officials cited decreased water levels as the reason for the cutoff.

item.title: Iran Raises Issue of Closed Shia Institutions with Taliban
item.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson stated that the country has raised the issue of closed Shia institutions in Afghanistan with the Taliban. Recent closures by the Taliban include religious, educational, and cultural institutions, as well as a clinic supported by Iran in western Kabul. Some officials from these institutions have been detained.

item.title: AI, Robots, and Drones Featured at Astana's AI & Digital Bridge 2026 Exhibition
item.description: Over 100 companies from Kazakhstan and abroad showcased developments at the AI & Digital Bridge 2026 exhibition in Astana. Highlights included humanoid robots, robot dogs, AI-based interactive technologies, drone races, and digital creative industry projects. Technologies spanned medicine, fintech, education, and cybersecurity.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Over 500 Million Tenge Paid to Patients Under Medical Insurance
item.description: In Kazakhstan, 502.6 million tenge has been paid to patients and their families under mandatory insurance for medical professionals' liability over the past two years. The Ministry of Health reported that as of September 1, 2026, 178,296 medical professionals are insured. Since the beginning of 2026, 1,867 insurance contracts have been concluded, with 112 payments made.

item.title: Fire on the roof of a five-story building in Kъonayev extinguished, 120 evacuated
item.description: Firefighters have extinguished a fire on the roof of a five-story residential building in Kъonayev. 120 people, including 30 children, were evacuated from the building. No injuries were reported. The fire was reported to the emergency services and spread to the roof upon arrival of the first units.

item.title: Fire in a multi-story building in Kъonayev, 120 people evacuated
item.description: A fire broke out in the roof of a five-story residential building in Kъonayev, prompting the evacuation of 120 people, including 30 children. Emergency services responded quickly, and firefighters worked to extinguish the blaze. The fire was fully extinguished, and no one was injured.

item.title: Kyiv Bridge Damaged in Russian Attack Shortly After German Chancellor's Arrival
item.description: A bridge in Kyiv was damaged by a Russian attack shortly after German Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in the city. Emergency services were dispatched to the scene. Merz is in Kyiv for an unannounced visit to discuss defense cooperation and German support, including significant military and energy reconstruction aid.

item.title: Latvian Prime Minister's Party Wins Election with Best Result in 35 Years
item.description: The party of Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kūlbergs secured 35.3% of the vote in parliamentary elections, potentially winning 42 seats in the 100-member Saeima. This marks the largest victory since the country's independence in 1991. Kūlbergs aims to form a coalition supporting Ukraine and maintain a firm stance against Moscow, emphasizing economic ties with Russia weaken the nation.

item.title: Afghanistan's Minister: Unjustified Shedding of Afghan or Pakistani Blood is Forbidden
item.description: Afghanistan's Minister of Rural Rehabilitation and Development, Abdul Latif Mansour, stated that the Islamic Emirate considers the unjustified shedding of Afghan and Pakistani blood forbidden, as both are Muslim nations. Speaking at the Wakhan road inauguration, Mansour urged self-reliance for Afghanistan to defend its citizens and stressed that the situation should not escalate into indiscriminate bloodshed.

item.title: Kazakhstan Paid Over 500 Million Tenge for Medical Errors in Two Years
item.description: Kazakhstan has paid 502.6 million tenge to patients and their families over the past two years as insurance payouts for medical errors, according to the Ministry of Health. The law on professional liability insurance for medical workers, effective since October 2024, covers 178,296 medical professionals. The mechanism allows patients to receive compensation for harm caused during medical care.

item.title: Kazakh scientist delivers lecture at Cambridge University on ancient Eurasian cultures
item.description: A Kazakh scientist presented findings on ancient Eurasian cultural ties at Cambridge University. The lecture focused on stone sculptures and the Botai culture, highlighting Kazakhstan's archaeological heritage.
